hook: The restless young man who became the greatest thinker of the early Church.

pages.x: Augustine was born in 354 at Thagaste, in what is now Algeria, to a pagan father and a Christian mother, Monica. A brilliant student, he went to Carthage to study the art of speaking, and became a teacher of it.

In his Confessions he remembers how, at 16, he and his friends stole pears from a neighbour's tree, not because they were hungry, but for the thrill of doing wrong. They threw most of them to the pigs. He spent pages trying to work out why.

As a young man he lived with a woman for 15 years and had a son, and joined a strange sect, the Manichees. He wanted to be good, but prayed: "Give me chastity and self-control, but not yet." His mother prayed and wept for him for years.

In a garden in Milan in 386, in tears, he heard a child's voice singing "Take up and read". He opened Paul's letters at random and read words telling him to give up drunkenness and lust. His doubts vanished, and Bishop Ambrose baptised him the next Easter.
pages.cap: Ambrose, the bishop who baptised him

pages.x: Back in Africa, he became bishop of the port of Hippo in 395 and served there for 35 years, preaching, judging quarrels and writing more than five million words. He died in 430 while the Vandals were besieging the city.

pages.t: Confessions and The City of God
pages.x: His Confessions, the story of his own life written as a prayer, is often called the first autobiography in the West. After the Goths sacked Rome in 410, he wrote The City of God: cities of men rise and fall, but the city of God lasts forever.
Augustine is the most influential Christian thinker after Paul. His ideas on grace, sin, time and the "just war" shaped both Catholic and Protestant thought for 1,600 years.
pts: Wrote the Confessions, the first Western autobiography
